notes: Restoration Hardware / rh.com. ACCESS: direct HTTP (requests + curl_cffi Chrome-impersonation) is hard-blocked by DataDome on every path tested, including robots.txt itself, first-level-category-sitemap.xml, /us/en/sitemap, and the /graphql BFF search endpoint (all returned 403 with a DataDome CAPTCHA challenge page) - confirms and matches the prior Furniture-pass finding. Playwright headless Chromium also returned 403 on the same DataDome challenge. Claude-in-Chrome (real authenticated browser) DID get past DataDome and was used for the actual investigation; robots.txt fetched via it carries NO Claude-specific disallow (checked - only path-specific disallows like /catalog/sale/, */search/*, */graphql/*, */my-account/* etc, no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web full-site block). WHAT WAS CHECKED: full main navigation bar (Interior Design, Trade, Estates, Living, Dining, Bed, Bath, Outdoor, Lighting, Textiles, Rugs, Decor, Baby & Child, Teen, Sale) - no Bestsellers/Best Sellers/Top Sellers/Popular/Trending/Customer Favorites nav item anywhere; a full scan of every homepage <a href> (regex over best|popular|trend|favorite terms) returned no matches; footer link list (captured from the /us/en/sale page footer) also has no bestsellers-type link. Individual category mega-menu flyouts (e.g. Decor, Living) and RH's own internal site search could not be reliably exercised because this scratchpad's Claude-in-Chrome session is shared with 9 other concurrent workers and the tab group was torn down / reassigned by other workers on nearly every call (repeated 'tab not in Claude's tab group' and extension-disconnect errors) - this is a tooling/contention limitation, not a site block (every call that did land on rh.com succeeded normally). No candidate Bestsellers URL or nav label was found via the channels that were reachable. Given RH's known catalog model (single curated brand, membership pricing, no mass-market merchandising badges) and the prior Home-Decor pass's independent note that RH excludes 'Collections' pages and other marketing-style categories, this absence is plausible, but is reported as best-effort given the incomplete mega-menu/search coverage.
